run.question: Application-gateway server is returning 502 errors in the app-101 namespace. Please investigate.

report.summary: Investigation of the reported 502s from an 'application-gateway server' in namespace app-101 could not confirm the reported subject, because neither the namespace nor any gateway object by that name exists in the reachable cluster; the reachable environment is the otel-demo demo stack. Facts: the cluster holds only the namespaces default, kube-node-lease, kube-public, kube-system, local-path-storage, opspilot-readonly and otel-demo; a pod query scoped to namespace app-101 returned zero objects; across all namespaces 32 pods, 29 services and 24 deployments exist and none is named application-gateway (the only gateway-like workloads are frontend-proxy, an Envoy proxy in otel-demo exposed as NodePort 8080, and prometheus-readonly-proxy, an nginx read-only proxy in front of Prometheus). Every otel-demo workload is at its desired replica count with available=1, all 22 otel-demo pods are Ready with restartCount 0, all 26 otel-demo services have populated endpoint addresses, and no Ingress, NetworkPolicy or ResourceQuota objects exist, so nothing in the Kubernetes state shows an upstream shortfall or a refused connection behind a gateway. Two zero-replica ReplicaSets (prometheus-547d4cbb8, otel-collector-845f9747bd, created 14:36:29Z) were replaced by prometheus-9bc78b5f7 / otel-collector-69c9f9649 at 14:38:03Z / 14:38:02Z, i.e. Prometheus and the collector were rolled out ~2 minutes after install; this is a change during the window that I could not tie to any 502s. Telemetry checks were not possible: every Prometheus query and every Jaeger query in this Run returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, and pod log reads returned zero lines, so no error-rate, latency or 502 status evidence exists for frontend-proxy or any other service. Runbook application-gateway-troubleshooting was fetched and its steps were carried out as far as the tools allow: step 1 (find the gateway pod status) found no application-gateway pod and no app-101 namespace, only frontend-proxy/prometheus-readonly-proxy in otel-demo, both Ready; step 2 (gateway error logs) could not be completed because fetch_pod_logs returned zero lines for frontend-proxy, frontend and prometheus-readonly-proxy; step 3 (verify upstream services) showed all otel-demo deployments 1/1 available and all pods Ready with zero restarts; step 4 (check gateway configuration with 'appg -t') could not be carried out because no command-execution tool is available, frontend-proxy's configuration is baked into its image and prometheus-readonly-proxy's nginx.conf is mounted from Secret 'prometheus-readonly-proxy', which cannot be read; step 5 (review service endpoints) showed all 26 otel-demo services with endpoint addresses. No root cause can be named: the reported namespace and object are absent, and the evidence needed to confirm or refute 502s from the only gateway present (frontend-proxy) is unavailable.

claims.text: The cluster has no namespace named app-101; the namespaces present are default, kube-node-lease, kube-public, kube-system, local-path-storage, opspilot-readonly and otel-demo.
A pod query scoped to namespace app-101 returned zero objects at query time (total_items_processed 0).

No pod, service or deployment named application-gateway exists: the 32 pods across all namespaces, 29 services and 24 deployments contain no such object, and a name/label filter for 'gateway' matched only frontend-proxy-844799bcdb-q7f5n and prometheus-readonly-proxy-7567c75596-nwrxw in otel-demo.

The only gateway-like workload fronting the demo app is deployment frontend-proxy in otel-demo: Envoy image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.0.2-frontend-proxy with ENVOY_PORT 8080 and upstream env FRONTEND_HOST=frontend/8080, JAEGER_HOST=jaeger-query/16686, FLAGD_HOST=flagd, IMAGE_PROVIDER_HOST=image-provider/8081, published through service frontend-proxy type NodePort 8080->8080 with endpoint address 10.244.0.22.

All 22 otel-demo pods are phase Running and Ready with restartCount 0, started between 2026-11-23T14:36:29Z and 2026-11-23T14:38:04Z, including frontend-proxy-844799bcdb-q7f5n (start 14:36:31Z) and prometheus-9bc78b5f7-k84v7 (start 14:38:03Z).
All 24 deployments cluster-wide report desired replicas equal to ready and available replicas (otel-demo includes frontend-proxy 1/1 and prometheus-readonly-proxy 1/1).

All 26 services in otel-demo have populated endpoint subsets with pod addresses, including frontend (10.244.0.20), frontend-proxy (10.244.0.22), prometheus (10.244.0.26) and jaeger-query (10.244.0.14).
There are no Ingress objects, no NetworkPolicy objects and no ResourceQuota objects in the cluster at query time.

Two ReplicaSets with zero replicas, prometheus-547d4cbb8 and otel-collector-845f9747bd (created 2026-11-23T14:36:29Z), were superseded by prometheus-9bc78b5f7 (created 14:38:03Z) and otel-collector-69c9f9649 (created 14:38:02Z), showing Prometheus and the collector were rolled out about two minutes after install.

prometheus-readonly-proxy-7567c75596-nwrxw runs nginx:1.28.0-alpine with an nginx.conf and /etc/opspilot-proxy mounted read-only from Secret 'prometheus-readonly-proxy'; its pod is Ready with restartCount 0 and probes are plain tcpSocket checks on port 8080, so pod readiness does not prove that its proxied requests succeed.

The gateway-like workload shows no Kubernetes-level failure: frontend-proxy-844799bcdb-q7f5n is Ready with restartCount 0 and no lastState termination, its deployment reports available=1, and its service has an endpoint address — none of the pod failure, eviction or OOM signals appear for it.

Upstream unavailability inside otel-demo (a backed-off or unready backend behind the proxy) as the cause of 502s is rejected by the Kubernetes evidence: every deployment is at full available replicas, every pod is Ready with zero restarts, and all 26 services have endpoint addresses.

Namespace-level network or quota misconfiguration (missing endpoints, NetworkPolicy blocking, ResourceQuota exhaustion) as the cause is rejected: no NetworkPolicy or ResourceQuota objects exist and every otel-demo service has endpoint addresses.

The reported entity likely belongs to a different environment: no app-101 namespace and no application-gateway object exist here, so the 502 report cannot be mapped onto an observed object and the closest analogue is a different entity, frontend-proxy (Envoy) in otel-demo on NodePort 8080.

If the 5xx reports do concern frontend-proxy, the failure would be visible only in its own access/error logs or in 5xx spans, which were not obtainable this Run (pod log reads returned no lines and Jaeger/Prometheus were unreachable), so unverified.

The telemetry read path is a candidate symptom rather than a cause: every Prometheus query in this Run went through the environment's read path (service prometheus-readonly-proxy, NodePort 9090->8080, nginx whose config is an unreadable Secret) and every one failed, which is consistent with a gateway-style 502 in front of Prometheus but cannot be confirmed without the proxy's config or logs.

Confirm with the reporter which cluster and namespace the 'application-gateway' belongs to, and whether app-101 is a separate cluster not visible here, before treating otel-demo/frontend-proxy as the subject.

Restore or repair read access to the Prometheus read path and Jaeger (verify the nginx config in Secret prometheus-readonly-proxy and its upstream target prometheus:9090) so that 5xx rates and error spans for frontend-proxy can be measured.

Once log access works, read frontend-proxy access/error logs for 5xx/upstream connection errors and compare with the upstream pods (frontend, jaeger-query, flagd, image-provider) which are currently Ready.

gaps: No namespace app-101 exists in the cluster reachable in this Run, and no workload, service, deployment, ingress or pod named 'application-gateway' was found; the reported subject could not be located.

All Prometheus queries (execute_prometheus_instant_query for up, vector(1) and absent(up{job="prometheus"}); metrics_range_query for sum(rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total[5m])); get_metric_names; get_label_values; get_prometheus_target; list_prometheus_rules) returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no metric, error-rate or latency reading exists for this Run.
All Jaeger queries (traces_list_services, traces_search, traces_search_by_tags) returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no span, status code or 502 evidence exists for frontend-proxy or any other service.

fetch_pod_logs returned zero lines for frontend-proxy-844799bcdb-q7f5n, frontend-6c9bc688bf-ll8s7 and prometheus-readonly-proxy-7567c75596-nwrxw, so application-level errors (including 502s) could not be read; log availability itself is a gap, not evidence of health.
The Kubernetes events query across all namespaces returned no events in the authorized window, so no event-based evidence (Evicted, OOMKilled, BackOff, SuccessfulCreate/Delete) is available.

Runbook step 4 (verify gateway configuration, e.g. 'appg -t') could not be carried out: no command-execution tool is available, frontend-proxy's Envoy configuration is embedded in its image, and prometheus-readonly-proxy's nginx.conf comes from Secret 'prometheus-readonly-proxy', which cannot be read.

Whether the rollout of Prometheus (prometheus-547d4cbb8 -> prometheus-9bc78f5f7, 14:38:03Z) and otel-collector (otel-collector-845f9747bd -> otel-collector-69c9f9649, 14:38:02Z) changed behaviour cannot be determined: changes happened before the telemetry sources stopped being reachable and logs are empty.
The change_history integration is not connected in this Run, so no change records could be reviewed.
No conclusion about customer impact is possible: no request-level or error-rate data was obtainable.
next_steps: Ask the reporter to confirm cluster/namespace for the application-gateway (app-101 is absent here) and supply the exact 502 timestamp window and host/path.
Check the nginx configuration and upstream of prometheus-readonly-proxy (Secret prometheus-readonly-proxy) and confirm prometheus:9090 is reachable from that pod, to restore the metrics read path.
Once telemetry is reachable, query 5xx rates for service_name=frontend-proxy and its upstream operations, and read frontend-proxy plus backend access logs for the reported window.
If the 502s persist, capture a failing request's trace and compare the frontend-proxy span status with the upstream frontend span to see which hop returns the 5xx.
